items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Well you’ve done a lot of research, I can tell because you’ve recorded albums of Victor Young’s songs.

ctx.x: Yeah, to do it, exactly. And nowadays, you go into a studio, if you ever see one of these group things going on, they’ve got about twenty microphones on a kit of drums. I don’t know why. And then when they record these guys, they get these microphones, you know you’ve got a cello player, and you can hear everything — there’s a squeaking on the soundboard. You hear the guitar — you hear the fret, everything is going like this. It’s nutty.
Well you’ve done a lot of research, I can tell because you’ve recorded albums of Victor Young’s songs.
